keyProcesses.description: Surface Inspection to CAD: Using a surface model to compare actual part to the nominal CAD data and provide a graphic report showing the deviations between the actual part and the nominal CAD data (surface data). We can then use the measured data to perform a "best-fit" analyses showing the necessary shifts & rotations required to bring the part or point set into tolerance.

Capability Studies: To comply with IS0 standards and Six Sigma, a proven process capability (CPK/PPK) is required. Using a CNC CMM part program to inspect parts at precisely the same location on each part, process variations are accurately measured. Using a sample size sufficient to emulate the population, statistical analysis can be applied to determine the control limits of any dimensional characteristics.

Digitising and Reverse engineering: Creating a CAD model from an old hard model or a prototype part. Involves digitizing the part to provides the scan lines, point data and geometry. The scans, points and geometry are then exported to 3D modelling software to create surfaces. The original part is inspected back to the new surface model, which highlights any minor deviations, which may still exist. Any differences can then be corrected, ending up with an exact surface model replica which can then be used to create CNC toolpaths, rapid prototypes, FEA's, etc.

FAIR (First Article/prototype Inspection Report): Using collected dimensional the results are entered into the database/spreadsheet comparing the actual dimensions vs nominal dimensions. The full layout, along with any necessary detailed sketches, are supplied so that the client can make any corrections that may be required.
Geometric to CAD: Integrating CAD to produce excel data on a part/component.

ISIR (Initial Sample Inspection Report): A standard report containing dimensional information of at least 10 randomly selected parts from a production run. Recorded in tabular form correlated to a marked print where each dimensional item is sequentially numbered for future reference. A measurement is made and recorded for all dimensions on each of the ten sample parts. The high and low measurement results are then recorded and compared with the dimensional limits specified on the product drawing.
Marking out: Taking an unfinished part and using its CAD and/or Drawing data to mark out areas where holes, trim lines, bends, machining, etc, need to be made.
R&R studies: Reproducibility & Repeatability studies. Measuring in batches of a given quantity of components.

BasicLineOfBusiness: Vendor independent consultancy and specialists in information security management.
ProductsAndServices: Information Security, Business Continuity, Physical Security Audits, Government Accreditation (CLAS), Records Management
Profile:
Advent IM is an independent specialist security consultancy, focusing on holistic 'protective security' management solutions that incorporate information, personnel and physical assets. They work with clients across both the public and private sectors to implement best practice security policies, processes and procedures and understand security threats in order to address security risk.  Their services centre around the following key areas:

Information Security Management (ISO 27001)
Information is a critical asset for every organisation. It is therefore vital to afford it appropriate security. Security breaches cost UK companies millions of £’s every year, and it is not only financial cost that impacts but damage to reputation and client confidence. Consequently more organisations are exploring the benefits of implementing best practice information security management following the guidelines in ISO 27002.

Services available include:

  • Gap Analysis;
  • Risk Assessment;
  • Risk Remediation/Treatment Plans;
  • Statement of Applicability (SOA);
  • Policy Development;
  • Staff Awareness Training;
  • Management Presentations;
  • Pre-certification Audits to ISO 27001.

Our consultants are qualified ISO 27001 (formerly BS7799) Lead Auditors with many years experience of delivering information security services. Advent IM is also part of the BSI Associate Consultant Programme.

Business Continuity Management (BS25999)
The need for effective and realistic business continuity measures is becoming vital as we become more aware of the risks of pandemics, theft, power outage, flood, fire and terrorist attacks. Addressing the technology aspects alone and implementing disaster recovery measures is not enough. Consideration needs to be given to the people, physical and information assets that are critical to the survival of the business. Consequently more organisations are exploring the benefits of implementing best practice business continuity management following the guidelines in BS 25999.  Services  include:

  • Gap Analysis;
  • Threat Assessment;
  • Business Impact Analysis;
  • Strategy Development;
  • Business Continuity Planning;
  • Business Continuity Testing;
  • Staff Awareness Training.

Advent IM consultants include BS 25999 Lead Auditors and other trained Business Continuity practitioners. Advent IM is a Business Continuity Management Industry Partner.

HMG Accreditation Services
With HMG Standards and the Security Policy Framework now more closely aligned to ISO 27002, Advent IM information security expertise enables a fully holistic service. Services include:

  • Annual IAS6 Audits for the Protection of Personal Data specifically required by Central Government and its suppliers;
  • Development of Risk Management and Accreditation Document Sets (RMADS);
  • Risk Assessment & Treatment Planning following IS1 Parts 1&2;
  • RMADS Reviews;
  • Security Policy Framework (SPF) Compliance Reviews;
  • Security Infrastructure Design Advice and Guidance;
  • Codes of Connection Reviews;
  • CAPS Product Evaluation Advice & Guidance.

Services are delivered by approved CESG Listed Advisor Scheme (CLAS) Consultants with a minimum SC security clearance.

Advent IM have many years experience in providing information assurance and accreditation services to both local and central government, Police, NHS, NDGB’s and NGO’s and are fully conversant with HMG guidelines and associated regulatory and legislative requirements.

Physical Security
In the world of protective security, physical security measures are often overlooked in favour of IT security technology and solutions; but electronic security measures alone will not protect you from a determined intruder.  Advent IM provides a holistic, integrated and risk mediated approach that includes security design, reviews/auditing and commissioning services to assist businesses with their physical security requirements, whether that business is a government department, retail outlet, data centre, public access facility or part of the UK's Critical National Infrastructure (CNI).  Advent IM checks, visits and reviews benchmark existing security measures and procedures against industry or sector best practice.  Reports identify vulnerabilities, make prioritised recommendations and include budget costings where appropriate.  Services include:

  • Threat Assessments – Intelligence and security trained analysts determine all threats to your business, its assets and brand, including terrorist; environmental, criminal and insider threats, based on their Modus Operandi (MO), likelihood and impact. It is the foundation upon which all security planning should be based.
  • Physical Security Health Check (PSHC) - A PSHC is a high-level review of ALL physical security components for an organisation and includes a high-level Threat Assessment.  The result of the PSHC is a high-level report that describes each security component in turn and comments on its effectiveness and whether it is “Fit for Purpose”.
  • Protective Security Advisory Visit (PSAV) - A PSAV is used to review the effectiveness, need and status of a specific physical security component, such as a CCTV or Access Control System.  The work will identify if a particular security component is “Fit for Purpose” or, if not already in place, make recommendation and benchmark against the relevant best practice.  The result from a PSAV will be a detailed report that specifically addresses issues raised by the client, particularly where conformity to legislation is required
  • Physical Security Reviews(PSR) – A PSR is a comprehensive examination of ALL physical security components for an organisation including CCTV, access control, lighting, fences and barriers and the manned-guarding elements.  The result is a detailed report, supplemented with photography and prioritised recommendations.
  • Design & Commissioning – Providing advice and guidance on all security measures, including aesthetics and ergonomics, perimeter security, lighting, CCTV, access control and ironmongery including fire interface, intruder detection systems and integration of all security components.  All of these are measured against realistic scenarios.  Once the systems are installed, a thorough and sequential commissioning process is conducted to ensure the end product meets the requirement. 
  • Secure Area Designs – Reviews to determine security requirements commensurate with protective marking for secure areas. e.g. data centres, forensic laboratories, server and safe/panic rooms.

Advent IM consultants have extensive experience in safeguarding personnel, premises and high-value assets.  Many have a HM Forces Intelligence Corps background and are trained analysts. All hold current government security clearances and provide best practice advice based upon government guidelines, as well as International, European and British Standards. Advent IM consultants are also Home Office trained in numerous physical security disciplines.

PCI DSS Compliance
All organisations storing, transmitting or processing debit or credit card data are required to comply with the PCI-DSS Security Standard, or face fines of £50,000 or more. ISO 27001 (formerly BS 7799) can help you avoid the soaring costs of PCI-DSS non-compliance.

Many of the ISO 27001 controls map directly with the 12 requirements in the PCI-DSS. So, if you are already complying with ISO 27001 (BS 7799) or intending to, you may find compliance to PCI-DSS less arduous. Advent IM provide a number of services to assist organisations in implementing best practice security, following PCI-DSS requirements. Services include:

  • Gap Analysis against PCI-DSS and ISO 27001;
  • Self Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) Reviews;
  • PCI-DSS Non-Compliance Statement;
  • Risk Assessment;
  • Risk Mediation/Treatment Plans;
  • ISO27001 compliance/certification

Advent IM consultants are qualified ISO 27001 Lead Auditors with many years experience of delivering information security services and a thorough knowledge of PCI-DSS requirements. Advent IM is also part of the BSI Associate Consultant Programme.

Records Management (ISO 15489)
The first international standard for Records Management aimed at providing a framework methodology for implementing best practice processes and systems. Services include:

  • Business process investigation
  • Needs analyses
  • Inventories and retention schedules
  • System design and strategies
  • Implementation plans
  • Ongoing reviews and auditing

    Whether your goal is achieving certification, ensuring compliance with legislation or delivering best practice Information Management processes Advent IM are confident they can deliver the solution you need.

keyProcesses.description:
APT has its own acoustic pulse tube test facility, which allows quick direct measurement of acoustic performance of prototype systems.
It can be used as a development tool, internal quality control testing, and for validation against customer specifications. APT are the only company with the ability to supply and self QA acoustic tiles. We can model and predict how performance changes as a function of frequency, temperature and pressure. Frequency 3-9kHz. Temperature 1-30°C. Atmospheric pressure to 600psi - equivalent to a depth of 400m, with repeat pressure cycling. Fast Fourier Transforms are used to provide frequency domain measurement of acoustic performance.

APT are specialist polymer engineers who design and manufacture elastomeric materials with controlled viscoelastic properties.
The materials are for use in underwater acoustic systems, vibration control, elastomeric energy storage and shock mitigation. We work mainly with natural and synthetic rubbers and polyurethanes using casting, compression and transfer compression moulding to produce parts from 0.4mm2 to 4m2. We currently have 5 presses in our production facilities.

APT are innovators in advanced material technology and provide integrated design, development, processing and manufacture of natural and synthetic rubbers, cast polyurethanes, and thermoplastic materials. The dynamic properties of polymers are manipulated to give innovative solutions to acoustic and vibration control applications. By combining polymer chemistry and component geometry, systems can be tailored to meet acoustic and other performance specifications, such as operational frequency range, echo reduction, insertion loss, temperature ranges, creep, fatigue life, environmental resistance, and working life. Materials are designed to be integrated into a full, working, manufacturable system, ensuring functional performance and viability for manufacture.

APT has a strong technical base of experienced polymer chemists, physicists and technologists.
With over 70 years combined experience, APT can offer a bespoke rubber moulding service for a wide range of components, including component, material and mould tool design. The mould tools are designed in-house, and a local toolmaker in Malvern manufactures the tools.

APT is a specialist in the design and manufacture of a wide range of synthetic and natural rubbers, polyurethanes, and thermoplastics.
With a well-equipped manufacturing plant, APT can handle all aspects of the process from design through to production. With an extensive range of polymer processing equipment for solid and liquid elastomers, APT supplies a range of off the shelf materials and primers, and customised products for specific customer requirements, either in bulk or pre-weighed polymer sachets. APT carries out moulding and assembly of finished components, with parts produced from 0.4mm2 to 4m2. Over the last 4 years, APT has developed a process for rubber - metal fabrication, using appropriate adhesives and bonding.

We also offer an encapsulation service for electronic components, arrays, hydrophones and transponders.
Materials are optimised for acoustic matching or providing mechanical and environmental protection for embodied electronics. Materials have low viscosity to reduce air entrapment, allowing encapsulation of complex parts. Transparent materials are available to allow inspection of encapsulated parts.

keyProcesses.description: Arrow Marking act as a channel for polymers, specialist inks and ink stamp cutting machinery to the trade.
Flash stamps are made with a stencil process that results in a rubber sponge being covered in a thin plastic film to create Pre-Inked Stamps.

Photopolymer die cutting is used to create ‘rubber stamps’ swiftly by 
UV curing of polymer material, then washing the residue away. 
Used for Traditional Stamps (Rubber Stamps) and self inking stamps.

A individual stamp-printing dies are cut apart and "mounted." Mounting is the process of attaching the dies to traditional mounts and handles or convenient self-inking frames. The final step is to stamp an image on a piece of indexing stock and attach it to the mounts for quick and easy identification.

A original stamp copy is prepared with a computer and laser printer and also using the following software: Agfa Proset Image Capture, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop. In order to make a negative, for a replacement stamp, the original copy must be on vellum paper. After exposing it to Ultraviolet Light, the reversing film is sprayed with a water based developer solution, swished with a soft cotton pad and rinsed with water.

With a vast number of ranges, styles and colour finishes available, and with new additions being added on a regular basis, Azzaduzo can meet the furniture desires of the most discerning of customers.

A complete 2.5m or 2.6m run of wall and base kitchen furniture, in a variety of cabinet door colours and styles, including one wall cabinet with glass doors and worktops for the base units (except the sink unit). Children’s Furniture

Profile:
Broadlands Consulting is a management consultancy formed by people who like to solve problems and help clients to improve what they do. Whether our clients make products to sell or provide a range of goods and services for their customers, we have experienced consultants who understand your needs.

Many of our consultants have worked for large blue chip companies, public sector bodies or not for profit organisations. They all have real hands-on experience of successful project delivery. Because we understand how businesses work, we can provide straightforward advice and assistance where and when it is needed, in a timely and cost effective way.

Broadlands is a relatively new Company, but our people are certainly not new to the game. Our consultants have many years' experience - both as advisors and practitioners - and are working with our clients every day to add value to their organisations.

Management consultancy

We help organisations to solve problems. Improving what you do, reducing your operating costs, deciding which course of action to take, working with partners to achieve your goals or sorting out a tricky issue.

Often our clients know that they have a problem, but they cannot be sure what it is. We take a straightforward and honest approach to help you focus on what matters. Once you have made a choice, our management consultants support you to make things happen. No magic, no frills, just good advice and a determination to get results.

Performance Improvement

Change is a part of our everyday lives, but how often do you review the way you do the basics? A good deal of your resources will be devoted to things that you do on a regular basis. The bigger the enterprise, and the higher the volume of operations, the more financial value you have tied up in your underlying processes.

We have a team of people who are experienced at reviewing process and ways of working to improve operational performance. It may be about fixing something that does not work too well, reducing costs, improving speed of turnaround times, or just getting a better return on investment. Or you may have invested in new technology and just can't see a pay-back.

Change Management

In times of change, whether it's related to a new business venture or something over which you have no particular control, it's good to know that someone has been there before. We can quickly assess the challenge facing an individual or a business, and then give advice in a helpful and pragmatic way. So there is no need for you to chart unknown territory.

Our change consultants will advise, support and coach you, and stay with you for as long or a short a period as they are needed - your choice. We have supported large organisations through major programmes of change, as well as helping individual managers on a one-off basis.

Interim Management

Good people can be hard to come by, and when they are found, there may be a lead-in time before they can get started. Or you may need a pair of hands to deal with a tricky issue or project. We can help by providing an interim consultant to manage the business on a short term basis. Our people are experienced in their chosen profession and also have the benefit of impartiality.

Option Appraisal

Making the wrong choice in business can be costly, embarrassing and time consuming. Often it's just not clear which route an organisation should take. When faced with such a dilemma, our consultants can examine a selection of the potential options for you and come up with a balanced view of costs, timescales and risks. We will also work out whether the chosen option will deliver your strategic objectives, provide you with a return on investment, or both.

We then wrap this up into a Business Case and provide you with a set of recommendations to guide the way ahead. The whole process is one that engages the key people in your organisation, and if appropriate, a selection of your customers.

Service Transformation

No matter how successful your business, there are few organisations that can boast to be delivering to their maximum potential. Whether you have decided that major change is required, or you just want to tweak something around the edges, our consultants can work with you to identify the most appropriate course of action.

Where service transformation involves major change in systems, process and people, we use best practice models, diagnostic tools and techniques to support you to develop a route map to change. This helps you to focus on the things that make a real difference to your business, and to devote your time and resource accordingly. This includes placing the right amount of emphasis on people, process and technology.

By using our highly experienced team to understand how you organisation ticks, we can identify the actions that will support lasting change. Clearly, radical changes to any organisation need careful handling. Managing people's expectations is key, and needs to be established at the start of any change. We spend time with staff and managers, talking with them and explaining what will happen and how they can play a part.

And it doesn't stop there - we'll then help you implement the recommendations, and manage through the overall change.

Training and Development

Our training courses are designed to help you to develop your people at all levels and in all aspects of your business, including technical application. Benefit from more highly skilled staff with increased motivation, delivering a higher quality service, achieving better results, more quickly, providing your organisation with better returns on investment.

Our training is delivered by a team of consultants who are experienced practitioners in their subject areas, across a range of industry sectors.

Training delivery format:
  • In-house courses designed specifically for your organisation's requirements, with a programme tailored to your needs.
  • In-house courses provided for you and your partner organisations with a programme agreed between you to meet your joint needs.
  • Regional seminars and workshops on popular topics designed for a range of audiences with common needs.
  • One-to-one Coaching & Mentoring.

  • Legislation and administration training in Health and Safety, Housing, Housing Benefits, Welfare Benefits, Fraud, Council Tax, Recovery and Enforcement.
  • Equality and Diversity.
  • Training and Development for Middle/ Senior Managers including Individual and Team Development, Change Management, Project Management, Team Building and Innovation and Problem Solving.
  • Specialist training in Stress Management, Smoking Cessation, One To One Coaching, Goal achievement and Motivation and Assertiveness.

BasicLineOfBusiness: Consultancy in mechanical design and engineering: noise, vibration, stress & failure analysis, marine technology.
ProductsAndServices: Finite element analysis (FEA), Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis, cost and weight optimisation, noise and acoustics consultancy, industrial noise & vibration control, turbo machinery design and fault diagnosis, concept generation and mechanical design, licensing amphibious RIB (rigid inflatable boat).
Profile:
Coupland Bell Limited is a Coventry based engineering consultancy, which celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2007. The company helps clients improve their products and designs by reducing cost, improving reliability and eliminating noise and vibration. Specific areas of expertise include:

Machinery Consultancy
Coupland Bell provides stress and vibration consultancy and failure analysis for a variety of machines. They specialise in industrial power projects and gas turbines. Their expertise extends to other forms of turbo machinery, including marine propulsion systems, wind turbines, propellers and fans.

Concept Generation and Mechanical Design
Coupland Bell specialises in solving unusual mechanical design problems, which other specialists have sometimes declined. This may include computer or physical modelling, prototyping and testing.

They also help design agencies to validate and improve their new designs, by optimising materials and geometry. This achieves the best cost for production, while ensuring parts will not fail prematurely.

Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to predict stress and vibration patterns in components.  It allows complicated designs to be manufactured or modified with confidence and gives a full understanding of the limitations of parts. Virtual prototyping can be used to ensure that parts fit and perform as expected, before any physical components are made.  The finished electronic model can also be demonstrated to clients and used to generate further interest in new products.

Product Optimisation
The company also specialises in the optimisation of products using finite element analysis (FEA) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) modelling. These activities primarily address product cost and weight reduction, as well as function and reliability improvement.

Noise and Acoustics Consultancy
Coupland Bell provides acoustics and dynamics consultancy for a variety of commercial and industrial projects. They specialise in industrial power projects and gas turbines, offering a complete design service, to ensure contract and planning limits are met.

Their service may include datum surveys – to identify and quantify noise levels. Trouble-shooting is offered to identify and rectify industrial noise and vibration problems.

They have unique expertise in measuring noise in hot ducts, including engine exhausts.

They also provide general noise and vibration consultancy, helping their clients build equipment as cheaply and effectively as possible while still meeting stringent acoustic requirements.

Their experience in marine technology allows them to apply their noise and vibration expertise to marine projects, including helping clients meet the noise requirements of the European Recreation Craft Directive (RCD).

Marine Engineering
Coupland Bell has expertise in advanced propeller design, marine propulsion and sound emission. The company is developing a new craft combining features of a hovercraft and a planing boat, which can negotiate mud, shallow or fouled water in bad weather.

keyProcesses.description: MESH: Mesh Networks provide blanket wireless broadband coverage for community access across specific sites where there are limited options for broadband backhaul links to the wider internet. Wi-fi zones: Setup of WiFi hotspots so our customers can provide WiFi to their clients. This type of solution could range from single hotspot to major exhibition site Wi-Fi zones.

Installation: As well as carrying out the site surveys for WiFi feasibility – we are able to install the wireless LAN solutions. Providing reliable, rugged and secure wireless communication solutions suitable for a wide range of environments.

Surveying: Feasibility studies into how WiFi can be incorporated into a building to meet performance and security objectives. Reporting involves the number and locations of access points for optimal coverage of both 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands. Also verifying WiFi radiation levels and identifying any interference (from both WiFi and non-WiFi devices).

Do-little Principles

  • AGILE - “Deliver value quickly & be reactive to the changing world”  [Agile   Foundation]
  • RECYCLE - Use what already exists e.g. “Don’t needlessly reinvent the wheel” 
  • HOLISTIC - “Be inclusive and open to other dimensions”, e.g. people sharing their experience, processes, systems, knowledge & information.

  • PERATO – Get 80% benefit from 20% of the effort
  • POSITIVE - "Don't give me those negative waves" [Oddball from Kelly's Heroes]
  • SIMPLE “Simplicity is the key to happiness in the modern world” [Dalai Lama]. “Keep it simple, stupid” [KISS principle]. Given a choice the simplest solution is always the best [Occam’s Razor]. 
  • TALK & LISTEN - Talk to all the animals!  [Dr Do-little]. That quiet little mouse is likely the key to success.
  • TEAMWORK - A team is stronger than the sum of its individuals
  • LEARN -  Exploit the collective knowledge - [The Borg from Star Trek]

Our Logo has a message too!
It’s an obvious pun on the “Pushmepullyou” a weird animal from our name sake “Dr Do-little”.
Our logo reminds us that:

1. Everyone is different.
The Lion represents strength, courage & working together. The Donkey represents the individuality, fun, steadfastness & insight. All these characteristics (and more) are needed for successful change.

The Do-little team has this sort of diversity. We are stronger when we work together.

2. Look at the world from different viewpoints.
We live in a diverse world. Yet there is a tendency towards uniformity in every domain. At Do-little we believe that this approach limits opportunity.

We at Do-little take a holistic approach that ensures all viewpoints are heard.
Our business solutions are more successful & robust as a result.

3. Change only happens when people are hooked.
Change can not be forced on people. It is surprising how strong a Donkey is when it is being driven somewhere it doesn’t want to go!

4. Don’t be too serious, life & work can be fun!

Experience in Service provides in depth experience in IT management consulting and services via a network of partners in the US, Germany and the UK. It is the sole Northern Europe Agent for West Trax Applications LLC, the developers of the Benchmark Express  family of SAP optimisation and compliance services. These have been specifically designed to provide "C" level executives with accurate, objective, independent business management data, to control SAP ROI, TCO compliance and business alignment issues. The service opens up the SAP "Black Box" providing transparency that reveals opportunities to improve business productivity whilst reducing SAP TCO and ensuring ongoing compliance and continuous improvement. Results are compared with Best Practice, by industry, geography and business unit.

Organisations make great efforts to justify their SAP acquisitions on the basis of long term ROI and business alignment benefits. However, industry analysts such as Gartner, META Group and Nucleus Research have expressed doubts as to whether these benefits are in reality ever attained. One of the more common concerns voiced is the failure of organisations to conduct post-implementation reviews to track realised benefits versus the original goals.

According to SAP's own data there are some 23,400 SAP customers worldwide with 79,800 SAP systems installed and more that 12 million users. Many of these are world-class companies. Not tracking actual benefits versus plan may present serious compliance exposure. Regular post-implementation reviews provide opportunities to maximise the value of the systems to the business, by identifying potential sources of improved productivity and profitability. This is not a one-off project but an ongoing process. It is not an IT issue. It is a business management issue requiring the attention of the CEO. 

Benchmark Express services support compliance and optimisation in SAP production systems. Our analyses highlight potential risk management exposures such as loss of process and data integrity. Value management metrics examined include ROI, productivity, costs and performance. Detailed recommendations are provided to address deficiencies identified.

Most analysis focuses on SAP functional modules as opposed to business processes across modules. Benchmark Express shows how business processes have actually been used by users as opposed to how they were designed to be used.

Profile:

Frost Electroplating offer a comprehensive subcontract electroplating service to customers in the UK and Europe. Finishes include Gold, Silver, Tin, Copper, Nickel and Electroless Nickel.

The selection of the best plating processes and techniques for each project is fundamental to Frost's approach. The company offers a wide choice to meet the vast majority of its customers' plating requirements.
  • Extensive use of information technology produces a highly flexible and responsive service.
  • Large library and knowledge of product and plating specifications retained in-house.

    Electroplating Methods

    All three electroplating techniques - barrel, reel-to-reel and rack are offered by Frost. Barrel is ideal for the electroplating of small parts in quantity. Reel-to-reel is suitable for all-over  or selective electroplating of  pre- and post-press strip material with coil weights up to 500Kg. Rack plating is used for large or delicate parts which cannot be barrel plated.

    Electroplating Finishes

    The choice of finish depends on the performance, protective or decorative needs specified by the customer. Solderability and conductivity are two key performance requirements which can be achieved by gold, palladium, silver and tin finishes. Corrosion protection is usually provided by nickel or electroless nickel. All finishes need to be aesthetically pleasing.

keyProcesses.description: Process of identifying and segregating electrical failures from a population of lighting control units.  An electrical failure is any unit that does not meet the electrical specifications defined for such device.  In simplified terms, electrical testing consists of providing a series of electrical excitation to a lighting control unit and measuring the response of it.

There are three different calibration methods that can be used:
Paper strips are impregnated with a pH sensitive dye which changes color when dipped into the nutrient solution. The paper strip is then compared to a color chart to determine the pH level of the solution being checked. 

Liquid PH test kits work by adding a few drops of a pH sensitive dye to a small amount of the nutrient solution and then comparing the color of the resulting liquid with a color chart. 

Using a digital meter, it is necessary to simply dip the electrode into the nutrient solution for a few moments and the pH value is displayed on a LCD display.
Hydrogarden supply spare lamps and also act as distributors for Osram, Philips Lighting and Venture Horticulture who make the sunmaster lamp range.

keyProcesses.description: Flash stamps are made with a stencil process that results in a rubber sponge being covered in a thin plastic film to create Pre-Inked Stamps

An original stamp copy is prepared with a computer and laser printer and also using the following software: Agfa Proset Image Capture, Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop. In order to make a negative, for a replacement stamp, the original copy must be on vellum paper. After exposing it to Ultraviolet Light, the reversing film is sprayed with a water based developer solution, swished with a soft cotton pad and rinsed with water.

Individual stamp-printing dies are cut apart and "mounted." Mounting is the process of attaching the dies to traditional mounts and handles or convenient self-inking frames. The final step is to stamp an image on a piece of indexing stock and attach it to the mounts for quick and easy identification.

Photopolymer die cutting is used to create ‘rubber stamps’ swiftly by 
UV curing of polymer material, then washing the residue away. 
Used for Traditional Stamps (Rubber Stamps) and self inking stamps.

keyProcesses.description: Proof-of-concept trials, Simple, quick ‘look-see’ tests to determine whether a material can be machined or whether a type of structure is possible. These trials allow you to get a quick answer as to whether an idea can be taken further. These initial trials last no more than a day and are usually turned around within 1 week

Batch production, extends the prototyping phase and leads to the production of batches of samples/parts, typically few tens to few hundreds of pieces. This is usually done over an agreed time frame (days to weeks) to allow customers greatest flexibility in the evaluation of the parts.

Applications development, detailed evaluation of a concept which usually involves characterisation of a process, assessment of a manufacturing route and production of demonstration samples. This phase typically involves work lasting a few days, often repeated a number of times for specific developments.

Prototyping of devices, following on from development trials, small prototype parts/samples are produced to an agreed drawing or layout. A typical run may involve few tens of pieces, produced over 2-3 days.

Technical consultancy for customers to benefit from our extensive experience is all areas of microfabrication and technical advice and support is provided from basic design concepts right through to manufacturing issues.

Ethos: Londesborough has pioneered vehicle arresting equipment for over 40 years in close cooperation with both the Home Office and Ministry of Defence and many overseas government policing authorities. Londesborough was established in 1962 and became a PLC in 1994. The UK first company to collaborate with a University Science park (Aston), Londesborough Security Equipment has engaged in continuous Research and Development in world policing to produce new and improved methods of vehicle apprehension. The policy of Londesborough Security Equipment is that of continuous improvement of its products to combat the changing scene in crime involving vehicles. The company is steadfast in its resolve to provide quality and not cheapness in its products.
BasicLineOfBusiness: Design and manufacture of vehicle arresting and entrapment systems
ProductsAndServices: Vehicle arresting and entrapment systems such as bacchus, baleen, lazy tongs, tyre deflators, ski-net and others. Maintenance and spare supply can be also provided via an established network.
Profile:
Londesborough Security Equipment PLC designs and manufactures a range of Vehicle Arresting and Entrapment systems for the worlds Law enforcement Authorities and Military Forces such as tire deflating devices, road spikes, deflator spikes. Celebrating 40 years of design and manufacturing of Tire Deflation Devices The late 1960's saw the storm clouds of Terrorism about to break over the British Isles. A new kind of Urban warfare had arrived where the ordinary people were the targets for indiscriminate bombings and shootings. Londesborough were invited to join the Ministry of Defence and Home Office in providing solutions to several of the new problems which were arising, including the apprehension of suspect vehicles which may be carrying or involved in ballistic content. Around this time also, a new cult appeared, that of 'Joy Riding' invoking Police Chases. We opted to look objectively at the problem of vehicle apprehension, and within a limited time scale, we researched and developed and prototyped for trialling, a device which became known as the Scissor Barrier. We had settled on a piece of equipment which could be deployed from the roadside, and developed the expanding joined slats forming a latticework which could be hauled across a road to intercept a suspect vehicle. We fitted a series of tire deflating spikes along the lattice slats, which the specification required, and that the design of such tire deflation spikes would be specific to causing a vehicle to come to a standstill in not more than 600 feet, the spike would have the ability to pierce known tyres. The spikes were specifically designed in a hollow pointed design incorporating three sides which are razor sharp, the spike is hollow and has air entry slots along its sides, the shank is specifically designed to remain in situ in its cup receptacle and to not become disengaged during transport or use.Of the numerous spikes we designed, this configuration gave the best performance for the task. The concept of utilising the weight of the suspect vehicle to self destruct its tyres became an added bonus. The vehicle itself, when impinged by the spike did not behave erratically during the slowing down process. We got the geometry right of the scissor construction, and taking a look at the launching of the device, we designed a carrying case which was also its launching and recovery medium.Our first Patent on the Scissor Barrier was Granted in 1972. Getting such a piece of equipment to the front line in a short space of time was typical of our engineering capability, and producing equipment to excacting required standards which would give it, its legendary efficiency, gained us accolades from around the world. The requirement for 100% safety for the Police and Military Teams using the equipment was of paramount importance, resulting in changes to design which would have reduced its stopping efficiency by around 200 feet, but the agreed stopping distance was introduced by the Police and Military procedures for using the equipment, and this was successful allowing Police and Military Teams the required distance from impingement for the apprehension of the suspects in the vehicle. The Scissor Barrier was Classified/Restricted equipment through the 1970's and was on permanent Exhibition at the Classified Defence Equipment Display in Whitehall, London for 20 years, allowing many thousands of visitors from across the world the opportunity to see demonstrations etc for their own Countries. We dropped the name Scissor Barrier, during the late 1970's, it was generally thought that such a name did not give the equipment the prestige it deserved, and so it became known as the LAZY TONGS*. a name associated with the great Aristocratic families in Great Britain. In the United States, in 1972, US service Officers had seen the equipment in action and having foresight to possibilities in the US commissioned Battelle to procure such equipment for the US Armed Forces, there being no similar equipment being available in the US. We have maintained contact with Battelle with subsequent developments in this field of Policing. During the1980's Battelle advised that we Patented the equipment in the US, which we did. We had established an Agent in the US during the 1970's who sold around 1000 equipments,and introduced the equipment to the US Law Enforcement Authorities, and implemented displays of the equipment on US Television several times and also demonstrated the equipment in Times Square which was featured in the New York Times. 40 years of continuous life for a Product is a success story, whilst we are continuously developing new equipments, some Classified, our attention is drawn to automatic and robotic deployment of such equipments, and these will be on our website in due course.www.londesboroughplc.co.uk 40 years of Service to the Worlds Police and Military Forces in the establishment of Law and Order, and Homeland Security Programmes for many Countries/ 1967 - 2007. Integrated Vision Systems: Real Vision For The Real World

Machine Vision Technology is in the business of making our customers more successful by solving their problems with camera-based automatic vision systems. MVT is an independent vision systems integration company, enabling us to choose the best tool for your requirements.

MVT is an independent machine vision integrator. This means that we are able to choose any machine vision software and hardware for a particular application and can therefore give our customers a solution that closely matches their requirements.

We are able to provide both off-the-shelf machine vision systems and customised solutions to ensure that we can meet our customers' needs. Machine vision systems with customer-specific front-screens can give production line staff a clear message regarding product failures, reject rates and statistical process control in a format that is familiar to them.

Machine Vision

The core of machine vision is measurement (including microscope-based measurement), presence/absence checking, colour analysis and position-checking. The products to be checked by machine vision systems may be metal, plastic, rubber or even food such as pies or fruit and vegetables. We have the expertise to provide solutions to many diverse machine vision problems. We routinely provide feasibility trials to show a potential customer how a task may be completed. Machine vision systems are usually installed 'online' and do not restrict conveyor or production line speeds.

keyProcesses.description:
Powder Painting
This is an essential part of Mec Com’s complete manufacturing solution. Capability is provided by the investment in a fully automated paint plant consisting of In-Line Pre-Treatment, Drying Oven, Double Sided Powder Coating Booth and Stoving Oven. All these stations are linked via a fully adjustable over-head conveyor system.

CNC Laser
The laser cutting process uses a focused laser beam and assist gas to sever metallic plate with high accuracy and exceptional process reliability.  The laser beam is generated by a resonator, and delivered through the cutting nozzle via a system of mirrors.    
Laser technology has the following advantages:
High accuracy
Excellent cut quality
High processing speed

CNC Punching
CNC punching machine can take CAD sheet metal fabrication designs and produce profiles and holes in metal sheets up to 10 mm thick. Sheet metal CNC punched parts can be produced with CNC formed up or down formed plunges and formed threads, small bends and mark free edges. These machines can produce high speed CNC engraved part numbers, logos or product identification.
CNC punching can also produce louvres, built in hinges, electrical knockouts and countersink forms which can all be manufactured to bespoke sheet metal fabrication designs. Being able to process components from sheet metal materials from as thin as 0.4mm right up to 10.0mm thick in a range of materials from steel, stainless steel and aluminum

CNC Bending
CNC bending machine is a forming machine tool (DIN 8586). Its purpose is to assemble a bend on a work piece. A bends is manufactured by using a bending tool during a linear or rotating move

Welding
Welding & Brazing: 3 x MIG welding stations, 2 x spot welding machines

PROCESS CAPABILITY
At the enquiry stage a proposed forging design is developed and process evaluated.
On receipt of order the process study is re-evaluated before die and tool designs are established.
Die and tools are in the main produced in house although external sources are used to supplement capacity or to meet special requirements.

QUALITY
Customer satisfaction is a pre-requisite of providing top quality forgings. Mills Forgings were one of the first forging companies to achieve ISO9002 accreditation and are committed to continuous improvement through their ISO9001:2000 processes.

ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY
The Board of Directors recognises the responsibility of the Company and its employees for impacts upon the environment. The Company Policy, therefore, is to continually improve the overall environment within which it operates, endeavouring to avoid, reduce or control pollution wherever practicable and to comply with current legislation or regulation.

FORGING PROCESS
From induction heating the slugs are forged on mechanical presses, range 300, 500, 600 and 1000 Tons.
The forgings are trimmed, pierced, and hot coined as required on supported presses.
A master process sheet for each part controls all stages from steel purchase through to final despatch.

MATERIAL PREPARATION
Cropped or sawn to process requirements, with control of:
Size/weight
Crop or sawn finish.
Specification and cast identification.
Component identification.

MATERIAL PURCHASE / CONTROL
 Purchased from only approved sources.
Each delivery is checked for identification, and size, with random analysis checks.
Identified to Mills control system.
Stored internally.
And controlled issue.

One press employed. This method of manufacture creates a smooth grain flow within the material and creates lower stress levels than other cold forging methods. This reduces stress levels and leads to reduced fatigue failure.

Polymer types used include ABS PP HDPE LDPE EVA PVC & MDPE

Please see our website Naylor Specialist Plastics - leaders in our field for more details.

Why choose Rateoval for your extrusion needs?
  • At the very heart of the UK, using modern techniques from modern premises.
  • Rateoval have the expertise, to offer advice on everything from polymers to pipes.

    Rateoval Standard Materials and Sizes

    Rateoval manufacture extrusions in a number of materials as standard, so we can cater for our customers needs in an exacting marketplace, as always we liaise with our customers so that they know that whatever their requirements we will be able to offer help and expert advice.  Below is a short list of the materials and specifications for some of the most common materials available today.  However if you need more information on materials and applications then do not hesitate to contact us.

    LDPE - (Low Density Polyethylene) Has outstanding flexibility at very low temperatures, with very good chemical resistance.  Potable water grades are available.
    HDPE - (High Density Polyethylene) Is widely used for buried gas and water pipelines.   It has very low friction loss with excellent abrasion and chemical resistance.   Please note: Maximum service temperature is 80oC.
    PP - (Polypropylene) Has excellent resistance to most chemicals and high heat (as high as 110oC for certain grades) good abrasion resistance.  Please note: Generally unsuitable for outdoor use unless stabilised against the effect of UV light (Ultra Violet).
    ABS - (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene) Has exceptional impact strength, it is also non-toxic and is suitable for use at low temperatures (as low as -40oC).   It is light weight, easy to join with solvent cement and has good chemical resistance, this makes ABS an excellent choice for most types of pipe-work.
    PVC - (Polyvinyl Chloride) Is probably the oldest and most commonly used plastic today.  In rigid form it has a working temperature of between 0oC - 60oC and can be easily joined with solvent cement.  Flexible grades are used for a wide range of low pressure tube applications with food quality grades available.
    HIPS - (High Impact Polystyrene) Is tough, rigid and is available in crystal clear grades that make it the ideal material for packaging and point of sale applications.  It has a maximum service temperature of 75oC with only limited resistance to dilute acids or alkalis.  Not generally suitable for outdoor use. 

    All materials can be delivered in a variety of colours and additives for;
  • flame retarding,

Profile:
NDE Clarke Transmissions Ltd are specialists in the design, manufacture and supply of a wide range of Driveshafts and Couplings for the Vehicle and Industrial / Marine markets.

Universal Driveshafts.
As well as standard Telescopic Driveshafts we can also offer Double Joint assemblies, Fixed Length, Mid Ship Shafts with support Bearings and Short Coupled Driveshafts.

Applications requiring wide-angle Flanges, long slip movement and balance grades to G6.3 tolerance can also be offered. Our computerised selection programme allows us to offer complete Driveshaft systems with minimal torsional twist or customised stiffness to suit a particular system. Bearing lifetime, critical speed and t.v.a studies can also be carried out.

Universal Driveshafts Light Duty
NDE Clarke Transmissions light duty range of Universal Driveshafts covers SAE range 1140 to 1510 and the DIN range from 58 mm to 150 mm Flange diameter. This gives a torque transmission range from 150 Nm up to 3120 Nm. Mechanics style Joints are also available for off highway applications.

Universal Driveshafts Medium Duty
NDE Clarke Transmissions medium duty range of Universal Driveshafts covers the SAE range from 1510 to 1900 and the DIN range from 120 mm to 250 mm Flange diameter. This gives a torque transmission range from 4000 Nm up to 24,000 Nm. Cross serrated Flanges from 120 mm to 180 mm diameter also fall within the range and any combination of the above can be supplied fitted to any of our Driveshafts.

Universal Driveshafts Heavy Duty
NDE Clarke Transmissions heavy duty range of Universal Driveshafts covers the DIN range from 225 mm to 435 mm. Flange diameter, face key design Flanges are also available. This gives a torque transmission range from 18,000 Nm to 270,000 Nm.

Flexible Disc Couplings
Our Flexi-disc range of flexible couplings offers an unrivalled package of performance, features and versatility.
  • Performance. The Flexi-disc range of metal disc couplings can transmit torques up to 260,000 Nm and accept maximum bore diameters up to 370 mm. High operating speeds up to 24,000 rpm can be achieved with dynamic balancing.
  • Features. Flexi-disc offers maintenance free operation, zero backlash, torsional rigidity, low reactional forces, good chemical and corrosion resistance with stainless steel disc packs and no fretting corrosion.
  • Versatility. Flexi-disc offers a multitude of different configurations including single element, double element, close coupled, dropout versions, variable length spacers and is also able to meet API 610 and API 671 specifications.

    KUSEL COUPLINGS - How to cure the problem of torsional vibration
    The introduction of a Kusel Coupling into the drive train will alter the natural frequency outside the normal operating speeds (normally below). By combining the torsional flexibility of the rubber elements with varying degrees of damping a Kusel Coupling can be selected to suit almost any application. The Kusel Coupling comes with a multitude of different mounting options to suit any mounting configuration. The Couplings can be supplied complete with a Cardan Shaft to offer a powerful combination of torsional and misalignment flexibility, in one Coupling/Shaft package.
    Service and Repair
    Our Service and Repair division can service and repair all makes of Driveshafts and for each Driveshaft returned to us we produce a detailed report on the condition of all major components. Collection of Driveshafts from your site can also be arranged.

Ethos:
Paterson Photographic is a modern, innovative, manufacturer and supplier to Photography Stores world wide. As they move forward into the new digital era their ethos, in keeping with their long heritage, is to continue to support the professional and keen amateur photographer with black and white chemistry and darkroom accessories.

For the latest products and service see the website. Read on to find out how it all started or go to Maurice Fisher's Photographic Memorabilia for more on the Paterson legacy.

Origins of Paterson Photographic

The following is extracted from the Paterson Group International booklet CAT978, dated Autumn 1998.

1998 was the 50th anniversary of the founding of Paterson, the company that invented the developing tank spiral as we know it today and helped to bring home processing within reach of the masses. In those 50 years Paterson have gone on to produce an estimated 7 MILLION spirals and pioneered a large number of other darkroom products. And, like all great companies, it all started with one man - and a chance encounter.

In the 1940s Donald Paterson was very busy man. He held professional qualifications as a Dental Surgeon, Lawyer and High Court Judge. In his "spare" time he was a keen photographer, gaining an FRPS and regularly went on photo safaris in Kenya. It was whilst on safari that Donald photographed a snake slowly swallowing a rabbit that it had caught and marvelled at the way the snake's backward facing fangs prevented the squirming prey escaping. That evening while recalling the encounter he realised the concept could be used to make a self loading film spiral, with the "fangs" gripping the film.

Some months later he showed his design to photographic distributors R. F Hunter Ltd in London and they immediately ordered 500 reels. The rest, as they say is history and the seeds of the Paterson company were sown. Late in 1948 Donald patented the spiral and 50 years later, the only major design change is that the "fangs" have been replaced by stainless steel ball-bearings. Sadly Donald Paterson died in 1975 while attempting to save a young boy from drowning, but his legacy lives on in the company he founded, now known as:

In modern business, speed is everything.
Mobile technologies contribute significantly to the speed of business, allowing people to exchange information digitally. Existing back-office systems can be extended right out to the front-line users in the field, wherever they are.
Customers can find the right vendors faster. Companies can reach customers with their proposals quickly, from anywhere in the world. Businesses can interact with each other quicker, and more easily respond to new challenges in the marketplace. 
Mobile solutions make business operations more efficient by eliminating unnecessary manual data processing and administration activities.
Sales Force Automation
Sales team access up-to-date information via a Pocket PC wherever they happen to be, which means that accurate product, order, and stock information can be presented during the customer meeting. Orders can be taken and processed immediately.
The number of sales calls per day can be increased, delivery times can be reduced, and the customer can be invoiced earlier. There is no need to hold as much stock, and un-necessary paperwork is reduced. Managers have access to timely sales, work and performance reports.
m-POS (Mobile Point of Sale)
Mobile Point of Sale provides the user with a truly portable Point of Sale till which can be set up literally anywhere. It can be utilised for queue busting where people may line up for the purpose of paying to enter a venue such as the Cinema, railway station or food outlets.
Retail outlets can reduce the number of waiting customers at the tills during busy seasonal rushes, by serving them as they wait in the queues. Airlines, railway and ferry operators can use the mobile point of sale to optimise trolley services, e.g. buffet cart and duty free.
Sales transactions are generated electronically with cheque, credit card and multiple currency cash payment options.
Delivery & Pick Up
A Driver's entire day is driven and managed by a Pocket PC. Signatures and other customer information is collected digitally, and new collections / drops can be advised to the driver en route, avoiding the need to return to base for more instructions.
This leads to better customer service, more efficient loading plans, more pick-ups and deliveries per day, and paperwork is eliminated. Managers have access to immediate accurate work analysis, and vehicle maintenance management is improved.
Asset Tracking
Hand held computers with integrated barcode scanners enable management and tracking of moveable and fixed assets. Assets are easily identified, located and tracked. Transfer dates, valuations and locations can easily be audited. Warranty details can be extracted and preventative maintenance visits can be scheduled.
Asset history and service records are always available allowing reports to be generated on demand. An assets performance over its lifetime can be monitored, and detailed information can be extracted to assist disaster recovery.
Questionnaire & Survey
A questionnaire wizard allows customised survey forms to be quickly and easily created. Multiple questionnaires can be held on a single hand-held machine. Data entry errors are reduced, and printing / postage costs are eliminated. Data can be swiftly analysed, and activity / time can be accurately measured.
Stock Take & Warehousing
Hand held computers with integrated barcode scanners enable swift, accurate stock takes. Barcodes increase speed and accuracy of entry, and eliminates mis-identification. Immediate comparisons between counts provides timely variance reports. Transcription errors are eliminated as stock counts do not have to be re-keyed on back office systems. Stock data can be easily queried and searched. This system can also be used for Goods-In management and reconciliation.
PocketServe
PocketServe is an electronic table order system which allows the waiter to take orders on a mobile computer and then transmit them to the kitchen without leaving the restaurant floor.
PocketServe automates the ordering process, eliminates hand-written paper orders, reduces Human error, avoids lost orders, saves time-consuming order duplication, and reduces the time from order to eating. Customer service can therefore be improved whilst improving labour efficiency and reducing costs.
PocketServe sends food orders directly to the kitchen and drinks orders directly to the drinks section without the waiter having to leave the customer table, which means more time can be spent front of house providing great customer service.
Unavailable menu items can be communicated instantly from the kitchen to all staff. Waiters can immediately offer alternatives at the point of order – so there is no need to go back to a disappointed customer to re-take their order.
Order status can be tracked for each table, concluding with printing a bill and accepting customer payment. Managers can easily update menus on all mobile computers at a touch of a button, and can generate reports for sales trends, or to generate food supplier orders to restock the kitchen.

  • Anti-static
  • Resistant to ultraviolet light

Profile:
QM Consulting specialises in website accessibility designs, verification and training.

They are dedicated to ensuring that their customers next web changes produce pages that work effectively for ALL their visitors.
You can try out their service with a free accessibility summary report on a page of your choice.

In the United Kingdom, about one in six people have some form of disability that potentially affects their access to web site information. The sorts of problems relevant to web site access include:
  • Blindness
  • Dyslexia
  • Hearing Difficulties
  • Physical Impairment.
    The Disability Rights Commission (2004) found that 81% of websites failed at the most basic Web Accessibility Initiative levels, and under 1% achieved higher level compliance.

    Developments in the Law

    The Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) has been in place for some years. The act applies across the complete range of publicly available services and specifically covers websites. Awareness of this act is growing with legal action starting to be taken against providers who don't make "reasonable adjustments" to allow those with disabilities to gain access.

    What are the Benefits of Accessible Websites?

    Apart from keeping the right side of the law, an accessible web site has many advantages to your business:
  • More Visitors from the Search Engines.
    The search engines can find your words and information more easily and quickly.
    This also reduces the search engine's carbon footprint!
  • Faster Loading  - important for visitors using mobile devices and dial-up customers
  • Ease of use - people don't stay if they can't easily find what they are looking for.

Profile:
The concept was simple, - to create a dual purpose high performance road going sportscar, capable of outstanding results on road or track. With all-weather everyday practicality

Enter Peter Needham whose glittering career spans two decades of Sprint and Hill Climb motorsport. With factory support he notably developed the first V8 Westfield on which the famous Westfield SEight was based, then went on to create the 'Splinter' hill climb super sports.

But Peter always hankered after a true dual capability, all round - all weather car. Enter the Shelsley T2, which has now been in production since 2000.

Many years of racing development and design, have gone into producing this ultra-safe handling - yet very responsive light weight 2 seater. Yet no sacrifices to comfort have been made. The T2 sports fantastic all round visibility, wide opening doors which are operated with concealed solenoid operated buttons. The dashboard equipment plus excellent heater system is as used in the Rover200/25 series. Due to superb aerodynamics, the lack of wind buffeting means conversation is still easy - even at VERY high speeds!

This car has been designed from the ground up to suit the 'Fast, but Getting Slower' driver! The ride is very supple and produces natural safe understeer when pushed hard. The T2 reaches 0-60 in around 4secs, but the truly impressive part is the 50-100 roll on in fifth gear, providing true driving flexibility - and this car in standard trim will do 150mph.

Safety matters have been also kept to the fore of the design stages at all times. Not only primary safety such as good visibility and outstanding handling and braking etc., but also secondary safety issues such as high impact side protection door design, plus intelligent crumple zones front and rear.

However we are aware that minor incidents can always occur and it is to that end that the seemless body panels have been cleverly created, which can simply be bolted on as easy as any large scale production car.

Profile:
St. Pauls Printing & Label Company has been trading for the over 140 years and has a wealth of experience in producing all types of metal embossed and printed identification labels on various materials for all types of applications and industries along with metal stampings and pressings.
We firmly believe that product labelling enhances your product or service and ensures your company name is clearly identified as the manufacturer/supplier, and therefore for both branding, marketing and legal reasons product labelling and identification is a vital part of any finished item or service provided. Stamped with a sunk or raised design, nameplates are available in a range of finishes and metals together with a choice of sizes and shapes. Setup is low cost and any quantity, large or small can be catered for. We also supply sequential numbered labels for tracking identification.
Screen Printed labels are extremely versatile and can be printed on a varity of metals and plastics. This is carried out in-house by applying an image to a sheet of material or component by squeezing ink through a stencilled screen, allowing the ink to become bonded to the base material and form a permanent image. Ideally this process is used by us to produce Company branded labels to fix to security fencing at events and building sites and facility services. Screen Printing has excellent durability; it is highly versatile and very cost effective. This process provides the most vivid, colour fast image of all printing types. Etched and Anodised nameplates are very well suited to corrosive environments. The label can be sunken or raised and then filled with colour if required. Often labels that are displayed outside are anodised to ensure its prolonged life in all weather conditions.
We have an in-house die and tool making facility that utilises computer design, drawing and modelling followed by spark erosion, milling, pantographing and CNC engraving. We manufacture dies and forces from computer generated artwork, and are able to offer a wide range of custom made stampings and pressing tools.

Spinning

The company’s anodising plant includes facilities for alkaline electro-brightening for a high specular finish (mirror like finish), chemical brightening for matt or satin finishes, plus plant to produce colours black, green and gold.

Stockfield Manufacturing uses its own hydraulic press to tailor their spun products to meet the requirements of customer specifications.

Polishing of products manufactured from super pure clad material is carried out in the company’s six lathe polishing shop.

Stockfield can provide a variety of paint finishes, including air drying and powder coating with polyester, epoxy and polyester-epoxy materials for high quality durable finishes. Different combinations of internal and external colour can be provided.

BasicLineOfBusiness: Manufacture, design and assembly of process water cooling systems.
ProductsAndServices: Air blast water coolers, dry air blast coolers, adiabatic air blast coolers, air blast box coolers, air cooled steam condensers, refrigeration condensers, pump stations, air cooled chillers, air blast oil coolers, air to air plate heat exchangers, run-around coil systems, air heating and cooling coils.
Profile:
Transtherm Cooling Industries (‘TCI’) Limited is a family owned/managed business that began trading in 2002. Based in Coventry, the company manufactures, integrates, and maintains specialist ambient air based water cooling equipment designed to reduce energy costs and to prevent the spread of legionella and other bacteria. Collectively known as ‘Air Blast Cooling’, the equipment supplied by TCI is used in the chiller, process cooling, air conditioning, compressor cooling and combined heat & power markets.

TCI’s route to market approach is to target the supply of components and sub-assemblies to OEM’s (for them to incorporate in the final product/solution), system integrators, installers and resellers. This approach coupled with unrivalled pre and post sale support for TCI channel partners, has given rise to the company’s impressive sales growth over the last 2 years.

The range of products that have been developed over the last 5 years are all based on the principle of cooling process water with ambient air, this is achieved by the use of extended surface heat exchangers through which is passed the water and across which is drawn ambient air.  This method of cooling, when compared to refrigerated cooling, is exceptionally energy efficient. 

The field of application for these products is extremely wide including furnace cooling, engine cooling for generators, air conditioning systems and, in recent times, for use in reducing power consumption of refrigerated cooling systems (free cooling) with consequent reductions in carbon emissions and green house gases. 

Reducing energy costs is a major driver and selling benefit where TCI cooling systems can operate without having to rely on refrigerating coolers for anything between 65-90% of a year operating at 10-15% of energy costs – the benefit to the customer and the environment is obvious based on these statistics.  

TCI’s current product range covers:-

Adiabatic Coolers
For many years it has been customary to utilise evaporative cooling towers to provide water cooling in applications requiring water temperatures below ambient air temperature.  Unfortunately, whilst these are very effective in providing this duty, they carry a considerable risk of spreading Legionnaires’ disease through the development of the Legionella bacteria within the water circuits. 

Identified in HSG guidelines as being a safe alternative, Adiabatic Coolers have not always been viewed as a viable economic option as the key suppliers are unable or unwilling to design and build effective control systems. The result is that although hospitals and universities accept their advantages and improved infection control capability they have suffered from a higher water consumption and greater maintenance than is necessary because of this crudity of control – TCI have addressed these concerns. 

TCI saw an opportunity to maximise the benefits from their knowledge and expertise and have developed coolers and control systems which are widely regarded as providing market leading performance, ease of use, low maintenance and low lifetime cost of ownership.  Drawing from customer requests and market knowledge, TCI have been able to build in some exclusive and unique feature which ensure maximum performance coupled with good compliance with health and safety legislation contained in government document HSG L8 (The Control of Legionella). 

Some of the features and benefits that have been built into the design include:

  • No chemical water treatment required
  • No clean and chlorination – low maintenance
  • Minimal plan area – easy to install
  • Low operating noise levels – very relevant in some locations such as hotels/hospitals
  • Dry cooling operated for majority of year – low energy use
  • Ultra violet light disinfection for mains water sprays – eliminates legionnaires disease
  • Full control package – reducing installation time, costs & on-going maintenance.

    Dry Air Blast Coolers
    TCI are one of very few suppliers in the market able to offer a complete package incorporating control panels designed to a specification that enables integrators to install easily and quickly with TCI supplying, within the package, all necessary components leaving only an electrical supply and pipework connections to be completed.  For the installer, this makes for both efficient use of their time and, with few parts to integrate, far easier installation reducing any downtime for the end user. 

    Air Blast Box Coolers
    Again the core focus has been on supply of a complete package making the re-sellers job, quoting, sale and installation, as easy as possible.  The air blast box coolers are made as both standard and bespoke, either indoor compact packaged units incorporating pump, tank and sight glass and simple controls or as packaged units suitable for either indoor or outdoor sighting, that include bespoke control panel with digital fan controller, pump tank, sight glass, pressure gauge/temperature gauge, copper pipework, valves either side of pump and hinged access door for ease of maintenance. 

    Water Cooling Ancillaries
  • Steam Condensers – CHP applications
  • Air Blast Oil Coolers – industrial applications
  • Air Heating and Cooling Coils
  • Air to Plate Heat Exchangers
  • Air to Tubular Heat Exchangers
  • Run-around Coil Systems
  • Pump Sets for use with any TCI cooler or as stand alone units.

    In addition to the existing product lines, TCI continues to lead the field with the further development of both Packaged Free Cooling Units and Adiabatic Cooler products and their application to the market. 

    TCI has developed its service as well as product capability as a key influence in both winning and retaining customers in the face of overseas competition for product. The company boasts rapid and flexible response to customers needs added to which is a computerised selection of products & quotation facility developed by and unique to TCI that, together with the experience of its engineers, ensures that the optimum solution is provided for each application and the client gets a premier service.
EndCustomer: Power generation suppliers, genset manufacturers, air conditioning suppliers, hospitals, Universities, bottle and plastics manufacturers, landfill contractors, and numerous customers in the metalwork and welding industries etc.

CompetenceTransfer: Successful transition to an indirect sales model, providing sales tools and design and engineering resources to enable OEMs, system integrators, installers and resellers to maximise sales.

Since 1685 members of the Toye family have been using their skills to create fine identity products for both the civil and military markets.

The company has excelled in the making and stamping of medals and insignia in the last 200 years, and they possess great expertise in the application of vitreous enamel and enamel painting for insignia, medal and jewellery production.

Their craftsmen and women combine the traditional skills of working in precious and non-precious metals with today’s modern technology to produce a vast array of quality products.

The product range has expanded considerably over the years and now includes: medals, enamelled badges, civic & society’s regalia, ceremonial chains, traditional handcrafted enamels, corporate jewellery, awards, and trophies.

The company also offers a free design service; designing and manufacturing products to customers’ exact requirements, and excels in one off bespoke products and small run production. They are also able to undertake the specialised service of renovation and refurbishment of presentation jewels and pendants of office.

The Toye Group of companies also incorporates The London Badge & Button Company which has over 30 years of experience in design and development of fine silver-gilt and silver cufflinks for high fashion men's accessories retailers.

KJD Jewellers, also part of the Toye family, manufacture hand crafted, very high quality vitreous enamel on precious metal cufflinks, to supply Jewellers and high end retail outlets.

This proud reputation has been founded upon a total commitment to quality products, competitive prices and an excellent customer service, all backed by a consistent programme of investment. 

People  
The quality of their team has been paramount to Wildan's success. Training and development is seen as an investment, not a cost. This, allied with a continuing investment in technology, helps deliver the service quality and commitment that all their customers have come to expect.

Wildan Signs can call upon a vast wealth of experience and commitment at all levels of the company to deliver its service to clients. Most staff have been trained in-house by a continual training programme in order to deliver the service levels you need in a very competitive environment.

Quality   
Wildan Signs has never been tempted to lower the high standards which have been the bedrock of the company's ethos. Their extensive installation portfolio has demonstrated the economic benefit to operate a quality regime that only uses the best branded materials and that only allows goods to be delivered or installed if they pass stringent quality checks.
